title: A Life Without These People Around You Is Already a Success
description: By “around you,” I mean friends, a spouse, family, and colleagues alike.
content: ※ This post was carried over when I moved my blog. (Originally written: June 20, 2024, 23:52) Excuse me? An incredibly obvious point. By "around you," I mean friends, a spouse, family, and colleagues alike. The first kind of person who really drains you is someone who meddles in and obsesses over every little detail of your business or other people's business . You can tolerate a few small instances and talk to them, but if they spend more time talking about other people than themselves, there's a good chance they're an empty shell. People wired this way tend to make everything into gossip rather than speak sincerely, so if you seriously open up about your life, there's a very strong chance they'll talk about you behind your back elsewhere. The second kind is someone trapped in their own world . Byun Hee jae a spy? Taegukgi rally supporters reassess Byun Hee jae shorts I had to include this video because it's such a textbook example... As you can see in the video, you simply cannot have a person to person conversation with someone who is ignorant but full of conviction . The last kind is someone who sees everything negatively . Whatever you say, they pretend to be cool headed and respond with, "To do that, you'd have to...", "Wouldn't you need to do ... first?", or "I think you'd need..." They've never actually done anything themselves. They're no different from armchair experts who only know how to give unsolicited advice online. Talking with these people only chips away at your self esteem and puts you in a bad mood, so don't get involved with them. It might also be worth reading this and asking whether you fall into one of these categories yourself. It seems obvious once you've read it, but most people don't realize these are harmful ways of speaking and behaving. That's why, as the person speaking, you can preserve a relationship by being careful about how you talk in the first place. Specifically: don't be the first to bring things up. This is a method I've verified through years of experience. Generally, it's easier on your peace of mind to be the listener and respond along with the other person. And finally, here's the most important part. This applies online, to your parents, and even to your closest friends. Never be the first to tell someone about your plans.

title: Knowing Myself
description: Some people will recognize the image above, while others won’t know what it is. Anyone born in the 1990s probably knows it: Cyworld, the Korean social platform that came before Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, and Threads…
content: ※ This post was carried over when I moved my blog. (Originally written: June 17, 2024, 20:02) Cyworld Some people will recognize the image above, while others won't know what it is. Anyone born in the 1990s probably knows it: it's Cyworld. It was a Korean social networking platform that existed before today's Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, and Threads. Although the service ended in 2015, it was hugely popular with teenagers at the time. People uploaded selfies to the photo albums on their personal mini homepages and enjoyed becoming "ilchon"—close online friends—with their real life friends. Background music, best friends, falling outs, the ulzzang era of internet famous faces, "100 Questions, 100 Answers"—there are so many memories. "100 Questions, 100 Answers" was a way to introduce yourself, and many people filled it out as a standard part of their profile. Actually doing it took quite a while and could be a bit of a chore. But finishing it felt satisfying, almost as though a distinct sense of self had emerged. Now that I'm an adult, there are times when I can't immediately say what I like or dislike. Sometimes I even question whether the hobbies and skills I list on my résumé are things I truly enjoy and do well. That made me wonder: do I really know myself? I think the act of writing posts while running my Tistory blog helps me understand myself. On the bus today, it occurred to me that I may have simply adopted other people's dislikes from the internet. I hadn't actually experienced those things; it felt as though I'd been living under the influence of what other people said they hated. As I was thinking about what I disliked, someone bumped into me while passing by. At that moment, I felt annoyed: why don't people wear their backpacks on their fronts on packed public transport? Now, if someone asks what kinds of behavior I dislike, I can answer confidently and explain a situation I actually experienced. I've been putting a lot of effort into understanding myself lately. These days I say more and spend more time online than out in the world, and I feel that a lack of experience weakens the reasoning behind my words. Sometimes I wonder, "What am I even trying to say?" Things we learn without emotion don't last. Whatever we do, we need to remember what we're feeling in the moment and put it into action. That's one way to know ourselves. If I can define success as the process of getting to know myself, I think I could become a truly happy person.

title: A Realization
description: Today I realized something important. It’s a kind of unwritten rule that may apply everywhere: if you want to succeed, you have to do something of your own. ChatGPT, selling courses, or putting yourself out there to become an influencer are simply means to an end…
content: ※ This post was carried over when I moved my blog. (Originally written: June 10, 2024, 23:31) Today I realized something important. It's a kind of unwritten rule that may apply everywhere: if you want to succeed, you have to do something of your own. Whether you use ChatGPT, sell courses, or put yourself out there aggressively to become an influencer doesn't matter. Those are simply means to an end. As of today, I've firmly decided to do whatever it takes to make things my own and live with a sense of ownership. Why did I make that decision? Among the posts I briefly skimmed today was one titled 'Sulbing sold for 130 billion won'. I'd casually thought of it as just another food franchise, but there was more to it. After a few more searches, I came across things like 'Stylenanda sold for 600 billion won'. I was surprised and fascinated that familiar brand names were selling for hundreds of billions of won, not just a few billion or tens of billions. Wondering how they had achieved that led me to this thought. For a moment I also wondered, "Could that happen to me?", but concluded that as a salaried employee, I couldn't even dream of it. I cautiously drew a lesson from the patterns behind their success and from what I see around me. Take a startup, for example: the hardest working person in the company is probably the founder. Why? Because it's their own business. If every employee worked with the same mindset as the founder, that startup could succeed. There's a saying I like: birds of a feather flock together. Even if I rise to the same position as someone else and receive similar treatment, a closer look shows that people who put in the same effort find one another. I must never become complacent just because I'm standing on equal footing with them. And if I can't fit in with them, I need to take time to reflect on where my effort has been lacking. No matter how lucky you are, spend enough time with people and your true abilities will eventually show. Ultimately, this comes back to the importance of metacognition, which I always talk about. And what I realized today is the importance of ownership. Everyone probably dislikes having things taken from them. Let's think of everything as our own. We need to know what we currently have and keep training ourselves to strengthen and protect it. From that perspective, the thing people neglect most is probably time. Ask yourself, "Am I taking up someone else's time?" At work, finding things you can do to save someone else time is what makes you a good employee. Let's be grateful for everything around us.

title: When You’re Wondering Whether to Do It
description: “Life is a series of choices and decisions.” Everyone has probably wondered “Should I do it or not?” at least once. Today, I’m recording my thoughts on how to make that decision clearly and quickly…
content: ※ This post was carried over when I moved my blog. (Originally written: June 6, 2024, 23:52) There's a saying that "life is a series of choices and decisions." And everyone has probably found themselves wondering, " Should I do it or not? " at least once. I wrote this post to record my thoughts on ways to make that decision clearly and quickly. 1\. When you're wondering, "Should I do it or not?", just do it. 2\. If you're thinking, "Is it okay to do this?", don't do it. 3\. If you're thinking, "Is it okay to skip this?", you should do it. 4\. It's better to try something and regret it than to regret never trying. 5\. For example, even if you wonder, "It's so hot today—should I go to the gym or not?", going will leave you feeling good and proud of yourself. Another example: during exam season, you might think, "I really want to spend today having fun. Is it okay not to study?" You've probably ended up regretting that afterward, thinking, "I should have studied then..." 6\. If you look closely at the meaning of "life is a series of choices and decisions," those choices include our thoughts and actions. Those thoughts and actions produce further thoughts that shape who we are. We grow by going through more of this process of becoming ourselves, so regardless of the outcome, when an idea comes to mind, putting it into action is the right thing to do. 7\. I don't know how you found this blog post, but if you have something in mind, I encourage you to go ahead and put it into practice.

title: Never Try to Beat the Market
description: Since ChatGPT 4o was unveiled, many people seem to be wondering whether they will lose their jobs. Job seekers are even more frightened. I feel that way, too. I wrote this to organize my thoughts on preparing for the age of AI…
content: ※ This post was moved from my previous blog during a migration. (Originally written: June 2, 2024, 00:17) Since ChatGPT 4o was unveiled, many people seem to be wondering whether they will lose their jobs. Job seekers are even more frightened. I feel that way, too. I wrote this to organize my thoughts on preparing for the coming age of artificial intelligence. 1\. The term artificial intelligence was introduced in the 1950s as “making machines behave as they would with knowledge of human behavior.” The 1950s were not long after computers appeared, and the internet did not yet exist. 2\. Let’s look at the chronology of industrial revolutions so far. (The following was written with help from ChatGPT.) The First Industrial Revolution used the invention of the steam engine to replace human or animal powered production with machine power. The Second Industrial Revolution dramatically improved industrial and manufacturing productivity through electricity, oil, and the introduction of large scale production lines. The Third Industrial Revolution brought digitalization through computers and the internet, fundamentally changing how information was produced, stored, transmitted, and processed. The Fourth Industrial Revolution is merging the digital and physical worlds through advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence, big data, and the Internet of Things, driving innovation across all industries. 3\. The Third Industrial Revolution began with computers, but I think the internet was what allowed it to blossom. With the internet as its foundation, the smartphone , which made internet access possible anywhere, was able to open a new era. Among the world’s ten largest companies by market capitalization today, all except Saudi Aramco and Berkshire Hathaway are in businesses related to the internet or computers . These are the companies commonly called Big Tech. 4\. Similarly, I think the Fourth Industrial Revolution began with big data and the cloud, and artificial intelligence may be what sets it alight. There must then be something that can be built on AI, but I do not yet have a clear sense of what that will be. 5\. Looking at past industrial revolutions, progress has made life more convenient by addressing things that were difficult, expensive, or inefficient. That progress has also inevitably involved some people losing their jobs. It is an unfortunate reality, but it seems unavoidable. 6\. I feel that this reality is now approaching us. This industrial revolution involves technology that replaces people, and its ability to use big data and knowledge is particularly threatening to high paying jobs. 7\. Unless a profession allows people to demonstrate creativity, survival may be difficult. What should we do to become irreplaceable workers? No matter how much I think about it, we may eventually have no choice but to give up our place. 8\. Then what can we do? All we can do is accept it. A reality we cannot change through resistance is approaching. It is also true that this is a once in a lifetime opportunity. The AI era will create opportunities for some people. So I recommend learning as much AI technology as possible in advance, starting now. 9\. Never try to beat the market.

title: Simply Holding On Won't Make Everything Solve Itself
description: Life is a continuous series of countless choices and decisions. A life without choices is dull. At a crossroads, we all want to make the best choice, but it is difficult to predict whether our decision will bring the best result. And choosing one means giving up another…
content: ※ This post was carried over when I moved my blog. (Originally written: May 31, 2024, 23:50) Life is a continuous series of countless choices and decisions. A life without choices is dull. At a crossroads, we all want to make the best choice. But while making a decision, it's difficult to predict whether our choice will bring the best result. And because choosing one thing means giving up another, some regret or lingering attachment to what we didn't choose is inevitable. We need to learn to enjoy situations that demand a choice rather than fear them. Regret always comes later, so we shouldn't let that feeling overwhelm us and make us afraid to choose. We should try to keep regret at as much of a distance as possible and delay its arrival for as long as we can. If we learn to manage regret, it can serve a better purpose, helping us develop the ability to overcome our current circumstances. Don't stand by passively when it's time to choose. Whatever choice you make, it will lead you to the best decision.

title: Live with Intensity and the Determination to Be the Best
description: Everyone is given the same 24 hours. It may sound clichéd, but while life isn't fair, time is. And it is true that time, once gone, cannot be recovered. In that sense, who I was yesterday creates who I am today…
content: ※ This post was carried over when I moved my blog. (Originally written: May 30, 2024, 00:36) Everyone is given the same 24 hours. It may sound clichéd, but while life isn't fair, time is. And it is true that time, once gone, cannot be recovered. In that sense, who I was yesterday creates who I am today. My past actions and thoughts have come together to make me who I am now, and what I am doing now will shape my future self. Unless the world stops, time keeps moving, so we need to recognize that this very moment is both the youngest we will ever be and something precious. That is why we should value every moment and live with effort. Many people already know that they shouldn't waste time. But I often fail to appreciate it because I think of it as a gift I received for free, with an unlimited supply still to come. In particular, among the things we do on our phones, social media and watching YouTube seem to be common ways of letting time slip away. There are many ways to use time efficiently. If you have plenty of money, you can buy someone else's time. Paying for knowledge that someone spent time acquiring is also a way of buying the time they invested. One of the most cost effective ways to use your time well is to enter their league. In other words, you need to change your surroundings. If you're going to spend the same eight to ten hours out of your day anyway, it's much better to spend them with smarter people. By entering their league, you can gain many experiences and learn new things. Maybe that's why people try so hard to get into good universities and climb higher on the social ladder. Let's always hold firmly to the determination to be the best.

title: Why You Should Never Study Entirely on Your Own
description: This isn't a post telling you to study with ChatGPT...
content: ※ This post was carried over when I moved my blog. (Originally written: May 29, 2024, 02:21) This isn't a post telling you to study with ChatGPT... When we study or try to learn something, we have all kinds of options: teaching ourselves, forming a study group with like minded people, getting help through tutoring or classes, or working with ChatGPT. Everyone may have their own preference, but the thing to be careful about is not to take a completely solitary, lone wolf approach. I think metacognition is one of the important abilities we need in life these days. When you study alone, you can sometimes convince yourself you know something even when you don't. The same goes for investing: if you catch yourself thinking, "I'm a little special..." or "This time will be different...", take that as a sign that your metacognition is lacking. The more this happens, the more likely you are to be lenient with yourself and strict with others. To develop metacognition, reverse that way of thinking. Don't forget to be honest with yourself and more understanding of others. It's true that this is a great time to learn through YouTube and blogs, but there are things to watch out for. You must learn best practices from people with a proven track record. Especially when it comes to investing, it can be difficult to distinguish experts from individual investors. Even if you join a trading signal group, I recommend at least figuring out whether the person makes money by selling signals or by actually investing. Personally, when it comes to crypto investing, I think anyone who calls themselves an "expert" or "master" is someone you should definitely avoid. Never assume you should simply grit your teeth and study alone. In a competitive society, being compared with others and evaluated by someone else isn't unreasonable. Whatever method you use, develop the habit of reading officially released technical documents and posts on official blogs, rather than news floating around the internet. The best approach is to ask someone who is actually earning money in the field.

title: If You Weren't Born into Money, You Absolutely Need a Blog
description: I think a blog is truly essential in this day and age.
content: ※ This post was carried over when I moved my blog. (Originally written: May 28, 2024, 22:16) I think a blog is truly essential in this day and age. What kind of age are we living in? You can throw a rough topic at ChatGPT and ask it to write, and it'll whip up a post in no time. It translates everything even if you don't speak English, and even lets people who have never coded before write code. We're living in a time when anyone can start anything as long as they have ChatGPT. But the important thing here is not to write the same "predictable" posts anyone else could write. If you're writing by referring to something you found elsewhere, it's easy to see that your writing is predictable. ChatGPT learns from collections of data gathered from the internet and produces something that sounds roughly plausible. That's why, going forward, we shouldn't copy posts from the internet, lean on them, or pretend they're our own. Of course, similarities can happen by coincidence, but what I really want to say in this post is: "When writing, use your own brain as much as possible instead of relying on a tool." Using tools is a skill in its own right, but creating is something only humans can do, and I think it will stay that way. If you look at the top one to three occupations that are hardest to replace in the AI era, most require creativity. Conversely, the first occupations to be replaced are those involving routine work, and that includes professionals such as lawyers and pharmacists. But I'm certainly not trying to say, "Write blog posts so machines don't swallow you whole." Going forward, we need the ability to create something , and through that, to find something that carries our own distinct character . In one sentence, I think the idea is that we need to become irreplaceable people. And I think a blog is one of the easiest ways to present yourself to the internet. After going around in circles, I ended up starting a blog on Tistory again, but the platform doesn't matter. These days, even on Naver Blog, it's hard to earn 1 million won a month through AdPost, and people say most earnings come from sponsored advertising. On Tistory, you need to write 'well' about things people search for a lot to get picked up by Google's algorithm. Though there's been plenty of talk lately about Google's algorithm changing, too... Unlike before, we should now approach blogging as a way to "build a personal brand and our own value," rather than simply to "make money." The figures in the image above are from 2020, so it's probably safe to assume the thresholds are higher now. Working hard may get you from a dirt spoon to a bronze spoon, and even that requires working yourself to the bone. With polarization getting worse in Korea, reaching silver spoon or gold spoon status requires success in at least one of these: business, running a shop, or investing in property, stocks, or crypto. Even then, you need luck on your side. But if you have expertise or something that sets you apart, you can bring that luck a little closer. That's why the poorer your starting point, the more you need a blog that shows your own distinct character. Most importantly, you have to believe that if you consistently build up a collection of quality posts, one day it will pay off. Let's all start blogging with the mindset that if we stick it out to the end, we'll win.

title: Things to Consider When Writing Blog Posts...

title: Laws That Might Help You Sound Smart Someday
description: Reflections on what laws mean in everyday life and investing
content: You have probably seen book titles such as “Laws for Avoiding Losses in the Stock Market” or “Laws for Surviving the Real Estate Market” in a bookstore. The image above shows the definition of “law” in Naver's Korean dictionary. A “law” is something absolute . What we call a “law” needs to be interpreted and applied differently across fields and situations. Of course, a law can be broken. But it does not change easily. Laws are built on experience. That is why drawing on the situations in which a law arose can help us make decisions. If we know the definitions and backgrounds of various laws, a day will come, at least once in our lives, when that knowledge proves useful. Below are the results of asking ChatGPT for 50 famous sayings. Pareto Principle: Most results (80%) arise from a relatively small number of causes (20%). Murphy's Law: If a situation can go wrong, there is a chance that it will. Zipf's Law: The frequency of a word in a text is inversely proportional to its rank. Metcalfe's Law: The value of a network is proportional to the square of the number of individual users in it. Brooks' Law: Adding more people to a delayed project makes it take even longer. Conway's Law: A system's design reflects the communication structure of the organization that designs it. Feynman's Law: When there is no preparation time, costs are proportional to the time a physicist spends working. Fitts's Law: A law of human movement stating that the time required to reach a target is proportional to its size and distance. Linus's Law: The principle that “given enough eyeballs, all bugs are shallow,” mainly used in open source software development. Moore's Law: The number of transistors roughly doubles every two years. Hick's Law: The more options there are, the longer it takes to make a decision. Dunbar's Number: The number of stable social relationships a person can maintain is limited to approximately 150. Peter Principle: Within an organization, everyone is promoted to a position beyond their competence. Machiavelli's Law: Any means may be justified in achieving an end. Say's Law: Supply creates its own demand. Sturgeon's Law: Ninety percent of everything in any field is rubbish. Thompson's Law: Anything always takes more than twice as long to accomplish as expected. Ivy Lee Method: Improve productivity by writing down the most important tasks for each day and tackling them in order. Occam's Razor: The simplest explanation is usually the best one. Parkinson's Law: Work expands to fill the time available for its completion. Gestalt Laws: A set of principles in cognitive psychology explaining the basic ways people organize and understand visual information. Laffer Curve: The theory that tax revenue falls when tax rates are too high or too low. Matthew Effect: The rich get richer and the poor get poorer. Hofstadter's Law: Things always take longer than expected, even when the expected time is taken into account. Maccabees's Law: Given enough time, unexpected events are certain to occur. Morse Law: Mobile phone processing power approximately doubles every 18 months. Gandhi's Law: To bring about change, we must become that change ourselves. Amara's Law: We underestimate technology's impact in the long term and overestimate it in the short term. Ripley's Law: If something is unbelievably interesting, it is generally true. Erwin's Law: If an internet argument continues long enough, someone will eventually be compared to a Nazi. Deming's 14 Points: Fourteen principles important for improving quality management and production efficiency. Cameron's Law: There are always more things we have to do than things we want to do. Gilbert's Law: A person's intelligence is proportional to their environment. Goodhart's Law: When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure. Adams's Law: Everyone must design and build part of the bridge they need to cross. Drake's Equation: A formula for estimating the possibility of extraterrestrial life. Ehrhart's Law: Human time and energy are proportional to the complexity of the technology people use. Karmarkar's Law: Improvements in production technology reduce production costs exponentially. Krum's Law: User interfaces should be designed to suit users' abilities. Lovelock's Gaia Hypothesis: Life on Earth biologically regulates the Earth's environment. Robson's Law: People always struggle against time, and time always wins. Shellenberger's Law: The pace of technological change is limited by society's ability to accept it. Socratic Method: A way of deriving knowledge through questions and answers. Sparks's Law: Opportunity arises when preparation meets it. Wolfe's Law: Bones remodel themselves according to the stresses placed on them. Illich's Law: Productivity declines once its optimal level has been exceeded. Gerard's Law: People prefer things they can control. Jones's Law: Success breeds success. Kapfek's Law: Change always encounters resistance. Queen's Law: A poorly managed project requires three times the time and cost. Laws are products of the experiences people have accumulated over a long time. Then, do the laws of success that so many people seek really exist...? If you search YouTube, you will find various quotations from successful people and hear about the lives they have led. If you apply those lessons directly to your own life and follow them, will you become successful? No. The experiences and perspectives of successful people are certainly important and can offer valuable insights. However, your current circumstances and the backgrounds of those successful people will be entirely different. That is why there is no universal “law of success” that applies equally to everyone. Nevertheless, if we want to succeed, we must keep searching without losing heart. By continually exploring within our own circumstances and making the right choices, we must strive to lead meaningful, fulfilling lives. That is the life I will work toward.

title: Humans Are Thinking Beings
description: Personal reflections on thought, action, and the meaning of keeping a blog
content: As everyone knows, humans are born with the distinctive ability to think . We describe it as a key characteristic that distinguishes us from animals, and say we differ from them in many ways, including logical reasoning, emotion, and creativity. It has been quite a while since I last wrote a post. In the meantime, I spent a lot of time wondering what topics I should write about on my blog. Many people on YouTube recommend consistently posting about a single topic when starting a blog. The reason is the idea of a “money making blog.” Most people tend to start blogging with the thought, “If I am writing anyway, wouldn't it be nice if my blog could also earn some money?” You have probably seen someone on social media say there has never been an easier time to make money. Even self help books make becoming wealthy sound incredibly easy. Perhaps because we are exposed to so much of this kind of content, it can be difficult to tell what is real and what is not. Sometimes, though, it all sounds painfully predictable. “Should I quit my job and try YouTube?” “Should I write blog posts after work and earn some pocket money?” “I like food, so should I visit restaurants and become an influencer?” Anyone can easily have these thoughts, and say these things so casually. Humans are thinking beings. By making the most of this ability, we have built a better world and evolved to meet the future. Of course, misguided thoughts lead to misguided actions. But without thinking, we would not even know whether an action was wrong. Thinking is very important. But we should not stop at thinking; we need to act. Thoughts that never become action are no better than crap. Fortunately, thoughts are fleeting, so it is good to save them somewhere just as they are. Keeping personal notes is a good habit, but from now on, I intend to write my thoughts on this blog. Humans are beings capable of putting what they think into action.

title: What Does Living an Ordinary Life in Korea Mean?
description: First, here is what you find when you look up the meaning of “ordinary.”
content: ※ This post was carried over when I moved my blog. (Originally written: June 5, 2021, 19:30) First, here is what you find when you look up the meaning of "ordinary." Normal, without anything outstanding or unusual. Naver Korean Dictionary In English, it is "common," and its opposite is "unique," meaning special. Most people want to live an ordinary life. What does living an ordinary life in Korea mean? Study until your twenties and get into a good university, Get a decent job and buy your parents a gift with your first paycheck, Meet someone you like and get married, Have children and live happily. This can't be the definitive standard for an ordinary life, but for most Koreans, it seems to be the basic expectation. Living the way described above isn't something to brag about or an achievement. It's the baseline. Like reaching level 30 in MapleStory and getting your second job advancement, then level 60 for the third, and level 100 for the fourth. That kind of feeling... It's like the basic quests the creator built into the real world for us to complete as we live. Of course, I'm writing this with ordinary people in mind. People born with a gold spoon—or a vibranium spoon—in their mouths started with a completely different character setup, so they probably won't worry about this and won't read this post anyway. But living an ordinary life has become far too difficult now. Let's work backward. What does living an ordinary life in Korea mean? Have children and live happily → Soaring housing prices make it hard to find a home. Meet someone you like and get married → More people reject marriage, and the growing list of requirements for men makes dating difficult. Get a decent job → Fewer jobs and a tough employment market. Study until your twenties and enter a good university → An admissions system that's difficult to navigate without private tutoring. If we're talking about Seoul, you're ruled out right from the start. People weigh up so many things now—your car, height, appearance, personality, job, and so on— that even dating is incredibly difficult these days. A respectable job... I don't even need to explain how hard that is; everyone knows... To put it plainly, we've reached a generation where even an ordinary life is damn hard. Especially if you're a man, you have to work your ass off even harder... And instead of trying to live an ordinary life, let's try to become special. It's easier to be special to someone than to be ordinary to everyone. One day, without even realizing it, you'll find yourself feeling ordinary among special people. Life Lament OrdinaryLife

title: My Personal Thoughts on Generation MZ
description: Simply put, it means millennials plus Generation Z: people born between 1980 and 2010.
content: ※ This post was carried over when I moved my blog. (Originally written: June 5, 2021, 18:30) What is Generation MZ? Simply put, it means millennials plus Generation Z: people born between 1980 and 2010. (Generations born before the 1980s include Generation X and the baby boomers.) In terms of age, that means people ranging from their late thirties to their teens. Seen that way, there could actually be quite a severe generation gap between millennials and Gen Z, too. But I think the gap is relatively small in that both generations are familiar with electronic devices and IT culture. Then was the development of electronic devices what caused the gap between Generation MZ and the older generations ? It's just my personal opinion, but I think so. I think even people of the same age will see things differently depending on their surroundings. And I don't view the emergence of generation gaps negatively, either. Original image To give an example, these days, are more parents reading books to young children, or putting on children's channels on YouTube? Think how convenient it is for parents. A few taps of a finger stop the baby crying, cost nothing, and save time. Literally the best. Children growing up in the past probably had a set of biographies of great people at home. Naturally, kids who read those thought scientists, presidents, and doctors were cool, and often dreamed of becoming one themselves. Now that children learn about the world through YouTube, maybe that's why they want to become YouTube creators, livestreamers, and influencers. This image is no longer available. Of course, there must also have been a generation gap between the people who actually lived through war and the baby boomers before them. For generations who struggled just to put food on the table, went through industrialization and financial crises, and could only make money by sweating it out in factories, indoor white collar work naturally looked appealing. Lawyers, doctors, and other licensed professions were popular, along with civil service jobs offering steady income and a reasonable workload. Coming back to Generation MZ, here's how I'd sum it up: 1\. They are more familiar with videos and photos than with text. 2\. They are sensitive to trends and consider recognition from others more important than their personal values. 3\. They often don't know where they actually stand. I don't understand young people these days using words like YOLO and FLEX. When I listen to people around me who are like that, I try to hear them out, figuring they must have their own thoughts and circumstances, but it just sounds like excuses to me. I've heard that Generation MZ could be the first generation to be poorer than its parents. Whatever happens, it's a natural phenomenon, but this seems to be how the world is working now. There may be people who understand these changes, adapt early, and prepare for them. That thought is what made me write this post. Personally, when I see articles like that, I think "Wow... okay..." is about the right reaction. Something you can mention casually at a café or over drinks to fill an awkward silence? Isn't anything beyond that crossing a line? And there's no need to go out of your way to criticize them or leave nasty comments. title: Thoughts on Blogging in the 21st Century
description: Most of us have probably seen videos or posts like these at least once.
content: ※ This post was carried over when I moved my blog. (Originally written: March 23, 2021, 20:46) "One post a day" "Make 1 million won a month from blogging" "How to increase your blog views" ... Most of us have probably seen videos or posts like these at least once. And there have probably been a lot more people starting blogs lately. "Can you make money from a blog? Isn't that just because famous people are doing it?? I don't have the talent, and I think it's too late to start..." If that's what you're thinking, please just give it a try. It's still not too late. I'd been thinking about it and putting it off since last year myself, until it suddenly came to mind and I started writing this. A blog can make money. Because in the information age, information = money , directly. To put the main point of this post simply: 'Knowledge is power.' 'What you know = experience = knowledge = information = money' If you stubbornly hold your ground on your own because you hate the condescending "Back in my day..." culture, you'll eventually get left behind. Just ten years ago, there were older people who couldn't use smartphones, but in a few years, we may reach a point where people find it strange if someone doesn't have an electronic device. Let's start before it's too late. Whether it's a blog, YouTube, or something else, you should have at least one building of your own in the digital world. There was a reason adults kept nagging us to study when we were young. The kids who grew up listening to that became lawyers, judges, doctors, and instructors, and now they're all rich. What about now? As long as you know how to use the internet, you can learn to cook, use computers, or sing, beyond your schoolwork. Even outside what you learned in school, if you can search well enough, you can pass yourself off as a pretty convincing armchair expert. From your bedroom, of course. The point is that the information age is absolutely overflowing with information. So we need to learn how to take it in and interpret it, and develop the ability to filter out the right information, understand it, and make it our own. I've been part of the subordinate class under capitalism, but I don't want to stay there. Here's hoping I can move up into the ruling class...
